current_determination: A convex mixture of translated compact-group heat kernels provides a globally defined gauge-covariant and reflection-adaptable blocking kernel that is exactly Markov-normalized on the physical group and admits holomorphic continuation to the complexified group without any field-dependent normalization Z(U). This removes the zero-free-normalizer obstruction of YM-R22 if the kernel is treated as a raw analytic density rather than by taking a pointwise logarithm. Its weak-field quadratic form equals (a/2) sum_j w_j ||B-P_j A||^2, which decomposes into the desired average penalty (a/2)||B-QA||^2 plus a positive path-variance operator D. D annihilates pure gauge directions but generally has a dimension-four F^2 component, so the heat-kernel mixture requires a tree-level Wilson-coupling/field normalization calibration before the dimension-six remainder can be treated as irrelevant. The remaining analytic issue is small-time holomorphic growth: with t_k=g_k^2/a, complex growth is controlled schematically by exp(C a R_k^2) on a canonical complex radius R_k. This must be compatible with the Bałaban analytic radius while a remains large enough to retain the coercive Q^*Q term needed for random-walk localization.

D annihilates pure gauge fields but generically begins at curvature-squared/F^2 because path differences are loop circulations; therefore a tree-level marginal Wilson-action calibration is required.

Zero-free normalization is replaced by a coercivity-versus-holomorphic-growth window: decreasing heat-kernel concentration improves complex-tube bounds but weakens the Q^*Q coercive mass used in localization.
negative_results: The normalized heat-kernel mixture does not reproduce the pure M+aQ^*Q Hessian unless the path variance D vanishes.
